_meta.description: Broadway theater metadata: capacity, tips, and notes. Keyed by venue name (must match shows.json venue field exactly).

Al Hirschfeld Theatre.tips: Great sightlines from the mezzanine. The theater was beautifully renovated in 2003 and named after the legendary caricaturist.

Ambassador Theatre.tips: An intimate house for its size. Rear mezzanine can feel distant — stick to the front mezz or orchestra for the best experience.

August Wilson Theatre.tips: Formerly the Virginia Theatre. Good sightlines throughout, though the balcony overhang can cut off set pieces in the last few orchestra rows.

Belasco Theatre.tips: One of the most beautiful Broadway theaters with stunning Tiffany ceiling lights. The mezzanine offers excellent views at a lower price.

Bernard B. Jacobs Theatre.tips: A well-designed midsize house. Front mezzanine seats are among the best values on Broadway with excellent overhead perspective.

Booth Theatre.tips: One of Broadway's most intimate venues — every seat feels close. A favorite for plays. Built in 1913 and shares a wall with the Shubert.

Broadhurst Theatre.tips: Solid sightlines from most seats. The theater is slightly wider than average, which helps with views from the sides.

Broadway Theatre.tips: One of the largest Broadway houses. Despite the size, the orchestra has a good rake for sightlines. Front mezzanine is excellent.

Lena Horne Theatre.tips: Formerly Brooks Atkinson Theatre, renamed in 2022 to honor the legendary Lena Horne. Intimate feel with good sightlines from most seats.

Circle in the Square Theatre.tips: Broadway's only theater-in-the-round — unique and immersive. No seat is more than a few rows from the stage. A truly special experience.

Ethel Barrymore Theatre.tips: A classic Shubert house with great acoustics. Center orchestra offers the best experience. Named after the legendary actress.

Eugene O'Neill Theatre.tips: Wide stage and good acoustics. The front mezzanine center is a sweet spot. Home to many Tony-winning productions over the years.

Gerald Schoenfeld Theatre.tips: Excellent sightlines from the mezzanine. The theater underwent a major renovation in 2018 with improved accessibility and comfort.

Gershwin Theatre.tips: The largest Broadway theater — home to Wicked for two decades. Even rear mezzanine seats have decent views due to the steep rake. Arrive early for the lobby experience.

Harold and Miriam Steinberg Center for T.tips: Part of the Roundabout Theatre Company complex. An intimate off-Broadway-sized space that occasionally hosts Broadway-eligible productions.

Helen Hayes Theater.tips: Broadway's smallest theater — incredibly intimate. Every seat is close. Named after the First Lady of American Theater.

Hudson Theatre.tips: One of Broadway's oldest theaters (1903), beautifully restored in 2017. Ornate interior with excellent acoustics. The orchestra has great legroom.

Imperial Theatre.tips: A premier musical house with a wide stage and excellent acoustics. Center orchestra rows D-L are considered some of the best seats on Broadway.

James Earl Jones Theatre.tips: Formerly the Cort Theatre, renovated and renamed in 2022. Now one of Broadway's most modern and accessible theaters with all-new seating.

John Golden Theatre.tips: A small, intimate venue ideal for plays. The mezzanine is steep but offers surprisingly good views. Limited legroom in the orchestra.

Longacre Theatre.tips: A classic theater with a beautiful proscenium arch. Center orchestra is best. The balcony overhang can affect views in rear orchestra rows.

Lunt-Fontanne Theatre.tips: A grand theater with an ornate interior. Originally opened with a retractable roof. Good sightlines from the front mezzanine.

Lyceum Theatre.tips: The oldest continuously operating Broadway theater (1903) and a New York City landmark. Stunning Beaux-Arts architecture. Intimate and charming.

Lyric Theatre.tips: One of Broadway's newest and largest theaters, created by combining two older venues. The theater can be reconfigured for different productions.

Majestic Theatre.tips: Home of The Phantom of the Opera for 35 years. A grand musical theater with excellent acoustics. Center orchestra rows E-M are ideal.

Marquis Theatre.tips: Located inside the Marriott Marquis hotel — enter through the lobby and take the escalators up. Modern theater with comfortable seating and no obstructed views.

Minskoff Theatre.tips: A large modern theater in the heart of Times Square. Home to The Lion King since 2006. Front mezzanine has exceptional views of the full stage.

Music Box Theatre.tips: Built by Irving Berlin in 1921 and one of the most beautiful theaters on Broadway. Excellent acoustics. A favorite venue for both plays and musicals.

Nederlander Theatre.tips: Good sightlines from most seats. The mezzanine has a nice rake. Watch out for limited legroom in some orchestra sections.

Neil Simon Theatre.tips: A large house with a wide orchestra. Front mezzanine center seats offer the best overall view. The theater has hosted many long-running hits.

New Amsterdam Theatre.tips: Disney's flagship Broadway theater, spectacularly restored in 1997. Art Nouveau interior is worth seeing on its own. Excellent sightlines from the orchestra.

Palace Theatre.tips: Famously raised 30 feet in the air during the TSX Broadway development. Recently renovated with modern amenities while preserving its historic character.

Richard Rodgers Theatre.tips: Home of Hamilton since 2015. Good sightlines throughout. The front mezzanine is especially popular for a full view of the staging.

Samuel J. Friedman Theatre.tips: One of Broadway's smallest and most intimate theaters. Home to Manhattan Theatre Club productions. Every seat feels connected to the stage.

Shubert Theatre.tips: The flagship of the Shubert Organization, located on Shubert Alley. Home to A Chorus Line for 15 years. Classic Broadway experience with great acoustics.

St. James Theatre.tips: One of Broadway's grand musical houses. Has hosted many legendary premieres. The orchestra has excellent sightlines; front mezz is also great.

Stephen Sondheim Theatre.tips: Renamed in 2010 to honor the legendary composer-lyricist. A well-designed midsize house. Good for both musicals and plays.

Studio 54.tips: The legendary nightclub turned Broadway theater. Operated by Roundabout Theatre Company. Retains some of its famous nightclub atmosphere in the design.

Todd Haimes Theatre.tips: Formerly Stage II at Second Stage Theater, renamed in 2023. One of Broadway's smaller houses, offering an intimate experience for new works.

Vivian Beaumont Theater.tips: Located in Lincoln Center — one of Broadway's few theaters outside the Theater District. Thrust stage creates an immersive experience. Excellent sightlines.

Walter Kerr Theatre.tips: A beautiful theater with excellent sightlines and acoustics. The intimate size makes it ideal for both plays and smaller musicals.

Winter Garden Theatre.tips: A grand theater with a distinctive wide auditorium. Home to Cats for 18 years. Recently renovated with improved comfort and accessibility.
